instruction: We represent Praitir Baking Holdings, LLC, the buyer, in its asset purchase from Glailirt Artisan Breads, Inc. Before we go back to the other side, the client needs a clear picture of where the deal documents leave it exposed. Please review all six documents in the folder and send me a memo that lists each issue you find, where it appears (document and section), why it matters for Praitir, and your recommended fix. Flag anything you think needs my attention first.

rubric.text: The response concludes that Seller's representations and warranties, including the environmental and food-safety representations, survive only until about October 28, 2026, roughly eight months after Closing. It identifies the issue as located in APA Section 9.1 or TSA Section 1.1, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.
hints: sixty days after the expiration of the Transition Period

rubric.text: The response concludes that the 30-day window to object to the Closing Statement ran from the March 30, 2026 delivery and expired on April 29, 2026, before the May 12, 2026 board consent authorized the dispute, so the Closing Statement and Closing Inventory Value are exposed to becoming final and binding. It identifies the issue as located in APA Section 2.6(b) or the board written consent, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Buyer's indemnity of Seller under APA Section 9.3(c) for Section 6.8 employee liabilities is uncapped and covers Seller's pre-closing employee liabilities, such as accrued vacation, severance or WARN Act liabilities. It identifies the issue as located in APA Section 9.3(c), 9.5 or 6.8, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.
hints: before, on or after the Closing Date

rubric.text: The response concludes that the pending sale of Praitir's membership interests recorded in the May 12, 2026 board consent is a change of control that TSA Section 12.2 treats as an assignment requiring Seller's consent, which would let Seller terminate the TSA on ten days' notice during the Transition Period. It identifies the issue as located in TSA Section 12.2, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that, because the TSA uses the APA definition of 'Facilities' (which includes the Secaucus Depot), TSA Section 4.3 requires Buyer to reimburse occupancy costs of the Secaucus Depot, an Excluded Asset that Seller keeps. It identifies the issue as located in TSA Section 4.3 or APA Section 1.1, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Closing Date was March 2, 2026.
The response states that the TSA Transition Period is 180 days beginning on the Closing Date.
The response is a memo that presents each issue separately and states, for each, where it appears (document and section), why it matters for Praitir and a recommended fix.
The response identifies which issue or issues need the partner's attention first, by priority ranking or explicit flag.
The response claims that Buyer's 30-day window to deliver a Notice of Disagreement on the Closing Statement was still open when the May 12, 2026 board consent was adopted.
The response claims that the APA Section 9.5 Cap limits Buyer's indemnity of Seller under Section 9.3(c) for employee liabilities.
